The demonstration organised by the local branch of the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP) on 15 December 2009 in Muş was held to protest about the dissolution of the party by the Constitutional Court.

The application concerns the alleged violation of Article 11 of the Convention on account of the applicant's conviction for disseminating propaganda in favour of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan) through his participation in actions carried out during a demonstration organised by a political party.

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to six years and three months' imprisonment for committing an offence on behalf of an armed terrorist organisation without being a member of the organisation, contrary to Article 220 § 6 taken in conjunction with Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code.

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to ten months' imprisonment for disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), contrary to section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to ten months' imprisonment for using force to obstruct a public officer in the execution of his duties, contrary to Article 265 of the Turkish Criminal Code.
On 7 March 2011 the Court of Cassation upheld the trial court's judgment of 17 September 2010.

Following the entry into force of Law no. 6352, the trial court reduced the applicant's sentence to three years, one month and fifteen days' imprisonment for committing an offence on behalf of an armed terrorist organisation of which he was not a member.

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to six years and three months' imprisonment for committing an offence on behalf of an armed terrorist organisation without being a member of the organisation, contrary to Article 220 § 6 taken in conjunction with Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code.

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to ten months' imprisonment for disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), contrary to section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

On 17 September 2010 the trial court sentenced the applicant to ten months' imprisonment for using force to obstruct a public officer in the execution of his duties, contrary to Article 265 of the Turkish Criminal Code.

The trial court found that by taking part in an unauthorised demonstration which started following calls on Internet sites affiliated to the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), the applicant participated in demonstrations carried out on behalf of the organisation, constituting a violation of Article 314 § 2 taken in conjunction with Article 314 § 3 and Article 220 § 6 of the Turkish Criminal Code (no. 5237).

The trial court found, consistently with the decision of the 9th Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation dated 28 February 2008 (numbered E.2007/13527 K.2008/1265), that the applicant's actions in participating in the illegal demonstration and being part of the group shouting slogans in favour of the leader of the armed organisation and attacking the security forces with stones and Molotov cocktails constituted disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation in such a way as to encourage the use of violence or other terrorist methods, under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The trial court found it necessary to punish the applicant pursuant to Article 265 § 1 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) because the applicant, together with the group in which he had been involved, attacked the security forces who were intervening in the incidents in order to prevent their intervention and to obstruct them in carrying out their duties.

On 15 December 2009, a local branch of the Party for a Democratic Society (Demokratik Toplum Partisi – the DTP) organised a demonstration in Muş.

The demonstration organised by the local branch of the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP) on 15 December 2009 in Muş was held to protest about the dissolution of the party by the Constitutional Court.

The trial court stated in its reasoning that the demonstrators had gathered around the district branch of the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP) for a press conference organised by the DTP to protest against the Constitutional Court's decision dissolving the party.
The trial court found that the demonstration on 15 December 2009 had been organised in response to general calls issued by the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).

The trial court found that following intensive calls for action on websites known to carry news reports in favour of the terrorist organisation PKK/KONGRA-GEL, on 15 December 2009 at around 10.30 a.m., a press conference was organised in front of the 700. Yıl Mosque in the Bulanık district by the former Bulanık district organisation of the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP), in protest against the Constitutional Court's decision dissolving the party.

The trial court found that a group of approximately 1,000 people gathered around the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP) building and started an illegal march on İnönü Street, Mareşal Fevzi Çakmak Street and Şehit Üsteğmen Suat İshakoğlu Street with stones in their hands.

The trial court found that the marching group carried placards depicting Abdullah Öcalan, who is in prison for the offence of committing acts aimed at bringing about the secession of some territories under the sovereignty of the Republic of Türkiye from the State administration.

The trial court found that the marching group unfurled flags of the so-called KCK (Kürdistan Demokratik Topluluğu – Kurdistan Democratic Community) and the so-called YDGM (Yurtsever Demokratik Gençlik Meclisi – Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly).

The trial court found that the marching group shouted slogans including 'PKK Revenge', 'Long Live Leader Apo', 'A tooth for a tooth, blood for blood, we're with you Öcalan', 'Again and again revolt, our leader Öcalan', 'A thousand greetings to İmralı', 'PKK is the people, the people are here', 'Bulanık plain, the home of the Apoists', and 'Who are we, we are Apoists'.
The trial court found that the group caused damage by throwing stones and setting fire to workplaces, particularly T.C. Ziraat Bank, Halkbank, and a shop called 'Mardin Manifatura'.
The trial court found that the group actively resisted by throwing stones and bottles at the security officers who were trying to impede them.
The trial court found that five security officers were injured by stones and bottles during the incidents in the Bulanık district.

The trial court found that the applicant directed the group which had gathered in the centre of the Bulanık district in response to calls by the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), using as an excuse the Constitutional Court's decision dissolving the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP).

The trial court found that the applicant's police statement — that he had not thrown stones at the police officers, had not provoked anybody, and that no one near him had thrown stones at the security forces — was not credible in light of the video footage.

The trial court found from the video footage that the applicant, standing next to people heading towards the police panzer, raised his right hand into the air and pointed at the security forces with his index finger.
The trial court found from the video footage that the demonstrators threw stones at the security forces, after which gas bombs were thrown and the demonstrators started to disperse.
The trial court found that the group which the applicant had directed with his hand threw stones at the police panzer and the security forces.

The trial court found that the applicant's testimony to the public prosecutor — that he was raising his arm to tell the group not to throw stones — was not credible in the context of the video footage.

The trial court found that a general call by the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan) was consolidated through material published and calls issued by the organisation's media outlets, and that such a call does not need to be made to a specific person.

The trial court found that the demonstrations on 15 December 2009 took place with the knowledge of and at the request of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan) and were carried out on behalf of the organisation.

The trial court found that by taking part in an unauthorised demonstration which started following calls on Internet sites affiliated to the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), the applicant participated in demonstrations carried out on behalf of the organisation, constituting a violation of Article 314 § 2 taken in conjunction with Article 314 § 3 and Article 220 § 6 of the Turkish Criminal Code (no. 5237).

The trial court found, consistently with the decision of the 9th Criminal Division of the Court of Cassation dated 28 February 2008 (numbered E.2007/13527 K.2008/1265), that the applicant's actions in participating in the illegal demonstration and being part of the group shouting slogans in favour of the leader of the armed organisation and attacking the security forces with stones and Molotov cocktails constituted disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation in such a way as to encourage the use of violence or other terrorist methods, under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The trial court found it necessary to punish the applicant pursuant to Article 265 § 1 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) because the applicant, together with the group in which he had been involved, attacked the security forces who were intervening in the incidents in order to prevent their intervention and to obstruct them in carrying out their duties.
